question: If statistics worked so well for Oakland, why couldn't the advantage last?
answer: Because good ideas get copied. Lewis ends with the Boston Red Sox offering Beane a record contract, then hiring Bill James himself, as rivals began to use the same numbers. An edge that comes from knowing what others don't lasts only until they know it too.
move: An edge built on knowing more lasts until others learn.
simply: A secret shortcut to school saves time until everyone finds out about it. Then the shortcut is just as crowded as the main road.
why: Any advantage from a clever insight, in investing, business or sport, shrinks as others copy it. The lasting edge is to keep learning faster than they do.
reference: Michael Lewis, Moneyball: The Art of Winning an Unfair Game (W. W. Norton, 2003), ch. 12
